# STEADY_STATE trajectory reference fixtures

The `.mod` files and CSVs are frozen native Dynare outputs; tests read the
CSVs unconditionally. They are not generated by puremacro.

The original minimal, RBC, and exact-endval fixtures were generated on
2026-10-21 using MATLAB R2026a and Dynare 8-unstable (2026-05-26 build).

`endval_literal.mod` and `endval_solved.mod` were generated on 2026-10-22
using MATLAB R2026a and Dynare
`8-unstable-2026-05-26-1801-f6a469d4`. Both specify terminal endogenous
values of 3 and a permanent innovation of 0.5, whose equilibrium output
is 2. The literal case leaves `STEADY_STATE(y)` at 3; the case with a
subsequent `steady` command recomputes it as 2. This distinguishes the
two semantics, unlike terminal values that already equal equilibrium.

To regenerate each reference in MATLAB with Dynare on the path:

```matlab
dynare endval_literal.mod noclearall;
writetable(array2table(oo_.endo_simul', ...
    'VariableNames', cellstr(M_.endo_names)), ...
    'endval_literal_dynare_out.csv');
dynare endval_solved.mod noclearall;
writetable(array2table(oo_.endo_simul', ...
    'VariableNames', cellstr(M_.endo_names)), ...
    'endval_solved_dynare_out.csv');
```

The first CSV row is the historical condition. Subsequent rows are the
ten simulation periods. These backward-looking models have no separate
terminal lead row. The native logs report a successful perfect-foresight
solution for both cases and print terminal reference vectors `[3; 3]`
and `[2; 2]`. MATLAB subsequently crashed during process shutdown; both
complete reference outputs had already been written.

`exo_steady.mod` is a negative reference. The same native Dynare preprocessor
rejects an exogenous variable inside `STEADY_STATE`, before simulation.
`exo_steady_dynare_error.txt` preserves its diagnostic. Regenerate it with
`dynare-preprocessor exo_steady.mod`; the expected process exit code is 1.
puremacro rejects this construct too, including shocks hidden by model-local
variables, rather than assigning them an artificial zero steady state.

The terminal interpretation follows the official
[Dynare reference manual](https://www.dynare.org/manual/the-model-file.html),
sections on the `STEADY_STATE` operator and initial/terminal conditions.
